subject: SIG: identity assurance - clarifications on SSO/SCIM/RBAC/MFA
messages:
From: Laura Jenkins <laura.jenkins@acme-retail.com>
To: sean_gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: security-team@acme-retail.com, devops_lead@acme-retail.com
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SIG Qs — SSO attributes, SCIM deprovisioning, RBAC defaults, MFA enforcement

Hi Sean —

Thanks for taking the SIG questionnaire. We're working through the identity/access portion and have a few follow-ups from our security team so we can complete the control responses:

1) SSO/SAML: Which assertion attributes does Redwood consume by default (nameID format, email, groups, department)? Do you require any custom attributes for role mapping? Also — what's the expected assertion validity window (NotBefore/NotOnOrAfter) you recommend?

2) SCIM provisioning: For automated provisioning/deprovisioning, what is the behavior on 1) user disable, 2) account deletion, and 3) group membership changes? Is there a documented SCIM schema and sample provisioning flow?

3) RBAC & least privilege: What are the default roles you ship (admin, operator, read-only, billing)? Can role membership be restricted to groups asserted by the IdP? How do you handle temporary elevation or just-in-time roles?

4) MFA: Are your management plane and console protected by enforced MFA? Do you support IdP-enforced MFA only, or do you require Redwood-managed second factors for certain APIs?

5) Evidence request: Could you provide a short artifact set we can attach to the SIG response: SAML metadata, SCIM endpoint docs, a role matrix, and a short note on MFA enforcement?

Timeline: we're hoping to finalize the SIG by Friday (2026-11-06). Can you confirm what you can deliver by then?

Best,
Laura Jenkins
Security Program Manager, Acme Retail

From: sean_gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: SIG Qs — SSO attributes, SCIM deprovisioning, RBAC defaults, MFA enforcement

Hi Laura —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick answers inline below; I'll attach the artifacts you asked for and loop in our identity lead for a couple of schema specifics. We should be able to get everything over before your 11/06 deadline.

1) SSO/SAML:
- Default attributes: nameID (email/urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress), email, givenName, familyName, and groups.
- Custom attributes: optional; we support additional claim mapping if you want to send dept/project attributes for fine-grained mapping.
- Assertion window: we accept NotBefore up to 5 minutes skew and require NotOnOrAfter to be within 5 minutes of issue by default — we can relax to 10 minutes by request for some IdPs.

2) SCIM provisioning:
- Disable: we set account status to inactive in our system within 60s of SCIM 2.0 replace/patch that sets active=false.
- Deletion: SCIM Delete results in a soft-delete retained for 30 days (configurable for Private customers) before permanent purge.
- Group changes: group membership patches are reflected within the same SCIM transaction; eventual consistency across services is typically <2 minutes.
- I'll attach our SCIM schema and a short flow diagram.

3) RBAC & least privilege:
- Standard roles: Owner, Admin, Operator, Viewer, Billing. You can map IdP groups to any role.
- Temporary elevation: we support time-bound role grants (TTL) via our console and API; entitlements are auditable.

4) MFA:
- Management console and API token issuance for human users require MFA. We support IdP-enforced MFA (recommended) and Redwood-managed TOTP as a fallback for IdPs that do not provide MFA assertions. Service accounts using API keys are not subject to interactive MFA but are protected by scoped keys and rotation policies.

5) Artifacts: I'm attaching SAML metadata, SCIM architecture doc, RBAC CSV, and a short MFA summary.

Next steps: looping in Karthik (identity) for SCIM schema details and Marissa (Customer Ops) to help with the role mappings and any contract-linked config. Karthik/Marissa — can you confirm the SCIM retention/purge window for hosted customers and attach any sample SCIM delta logs?

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: SIG Qs — SSO attributes, SCIM deprovisioning, RBAC defaults, MFA enforcement

Hi Laura —

Attached are the artifacts you can include with the SIG response:
- redwood_saml_metadata.xml (SAML SP metadata + attribute mapping notes)
- scim-provisioning-architecture.pdf (SCIM schema, provisioning flow diagram, disable vs delete behavior)
- rbac-role-map.csv (default roles and sample group->role mappings)
- mfa-enforcement-summary.txt (short note on MFA policy and exceptions)

Short summaries:
- SAML: we consume email/nameID, givenName, familyName, groups; optional custom attributes supported. Typical assertion skew tolerance is +/-5 minutes; we can relax on request.
- SCIM: active=false -> account disabled in ~60s; delete -> soft-delete for hosted customers with 30-day retention (configurable for Private deployments). Group membership changes propagate in <2 minutes. SCIM schema is SCIM 2.0 with Redwood extensions documented in the attached PDF.
- RBAC: Owner, Admin, Operator, Viewer, Billing. Group->role mapping is supported via IdP group assertions (see CSV). Temporary elevations are supported via TTLed grants and are fully auditable.
- MFA: console & human API token issuance require MFA. We trust IdP-enforced MFA. Redwood-managed TOTP is available as a fallback; machine/service keys are exempt but protected with scoped key policies and rotation.

Evidence links: I placed the artifacts in the shared folder here: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/Acme/SIG/identity-artifacts and included a DocuSign envelope for the mutual NDA if you need it signed before we deliver more sensitive logs.

Let me know if you need any redactions or a short cover note we can add to the SIG response. Happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
